title: Core database statement timeout and lock timeout (operator-configured; unset leaves Core's behaviour unchanged)
requirementRefs: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md Story 12.3 (traceability RES-18.x, QB-F; audit P1-03), orchestrator-approved slice 12.3a: statement timeout and lock timeout only
PRD/product-requirements.md section 15 row F (resilience and graceful degradation: dependency failures degrade explicitly, nothing fails silently)
PRD/product-requirements.md section 15 row R (one documented configuration contract per service)
PRD/product-requirements.md section 18 items 2 and 8 (dependency failure handling; no corruption after interrupted operations)
PRD/product-requirements.md PR-10 and section 19 (no requirement or target value is invented; database query behaviour targets are OWNER TARGET REQUIRED)
_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/epic-12-context.md Requirements & Constraints, Reliability: timeout values come from configuration and are never invented
docs/audits/production-readiness-2026-12.md section 5 (no statement or lock timeout in Core) and P1-03, as evidence only
architectureConstraints: fileRestructure.md: Go Core (services/core-platform) stays the only owner of canonical state; configuration stays in internal/config and the pool in internal/platform/postgres (MOVE/REFACTOR LATER, not moved by this story)
fileRestructure.md rules 9-10 and section 4.1: Prisma (apps/api/prisma) stays the only migration authority; no schema change and no migration
ADR 0001 item 2: PostgreSQL is authoritative and is reached only through Core's pool
No production timeout value is chosen: the target is an open owner decision (PRD section 19, OWNER TARGET REQUIRED)

acceptanceCriteria.given: neither SERVVIA_CORE_DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT nor SERVVIA_CORE_DB_LOCK_TIMEOUT is set (missing or blank)
acceptanceCriteria.when: Core starts and opens database sessions
acceptanceCriteria.then: startup succeeds and every session's statement_timeout and lock_timeout are exactly what they were before this change (the server or role default, or a value already given in DATABASE_URL)

acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator sets either or both variables to a valid value (a whole number of milliseconds from 1ms to 2147483647ms, written as a duration such as 200ms or 5s)
acceptanceCriteria.when: Core opens any database session (requests, workers, realtime, readiness)
acceptanceCriteria.then: the session reports the configured value for each set variable, overriding the same parameter in DATABASE_URL, and each variable is applied independently of the other

acceptanceCriteria.given: a configured statement timeout or lock timeout
acceptanceCriteria.when: a statement in a Core session runs longer than the statement bound (SQLSTATE 57014) or waits for a lock held by another transaction longer than the lock bound (SQLSTATE 55P03)
acceptanceCriteria.then: that statement fails instead of waiting and its transaction commits nothing

acceptanceCriteria.given: an operator sets either variable to an invalid value (unparseable, zero, negative, below 1ms, not a whole number of milliseconds, or above 2147483647ms)
acceptanceCriteria.then: Core refuses to start, in every environment, with an error naming that variable

acceptanceCriteria.when: an operator reads its Configuration table
acceptanceCriteria.then: both variables are documented with no default, unset meaning no bound, the accepted range, and the value being the operator's decision

acceptanceCriteria.given: the existing Core unit, contract, architecture and PostgreSQL/Redis integration suites
acceptanceCriteria.when: they run against the change with neither variable set
acceptanceCriteria.then: every existing test passes unchanged and none is skipped, removed or weakened; Prisma schema and migrations, contracts/, Nest and every other Story 12.3 surface (rate limits, dead-letter replay, metrics) are untouched

completionCriteria: Every mandatory check passes on the candidate with at least its minimum test count and no skip.
Each required test runs and passes; those marked expectBaselineFailure fail or do not run on the baseline with their sources placed on it.
No change outside the allowed surfaces other than new test files and the story spec's own status and logs; no forbidden or governance surface changed.
No default or production timeout value exists in code, configuration or documentation.
Acceptance remains the orchestrator's decision; device-route rate limits, dead-letter replay and metrics remain in the Story 12.3 backlog.
